You promise yourself that you will stick with horizontal breakouts but then you find yourself taking a trade here and there on diagonal breakouts...

Reason: frequency of horizontal setups.

They are less frequent.

and you want more trade signals.

Solution: expand your research universe. Review more tradable charts. 

I added the chart below to the #watchlist. Thinking that we might have the 3rd signal in the past 2 years. Imagine in the past 2 years, there were 2 clean horizontal breakouts on this chart.

But then you have 1000s of listed instruments in exchanges.

Note: horizontal boundaries are not magic. Breakouts through them fail as well. 

However, they are more objective in showing you the invalidation levels. 

Knowing when something is not working or working according to the book is the most important advantage in trading. 

It is the "knowing" with the help of "objective technical levels" that help you to cut the losses short and let your winners run.

Diagonal lines on charts are like the images you see in the clouds. 

They are there and then they are not there.

Whereas horizontal lines are there even if you open your charts years, decades after...

BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.1 percentage point in June, to 2.7%, the lowest since June 2022.

This marks the 5th consecutive monthly decline, bringing the cumulative drop to -1.7 percentage points.

This is also the 3rd-lowest monthly reading since April 2008, during the Financial Crisis.

To put this into perspective, the personal savings rate averaged ~5.5% between 2014 and 2019.

The only period in modern history with similarly low saving rates was 2005-2007, when the rate fluctuated between 1.4% and 3.3%.

US households are struggling to save money.

China’s economy is losing momentum:

China's manufacturing PMI fell -1.1 points in July, to 49.2, one of the lowest readings since 2023.

This also marks the first reading below 50 since February, signaling contraction in the sector.

At the same time, non-manufacturing PMI, measuring construction and services activity, declined -1.2 points, to 49.0, the lowest since December 2022.

Construction PMI alone dropped 2.0 points, to 47.0 points, the lowest since the 2020 pandemic.

On top of this, China’s GDP growth slowed to just +4.3% YoY in Q2 2026, the weakest expansion since Q4 2022.

China’s slowdown is spreading across its economy.

The US ETF industry is seeing unprecedented growth:

There have been ~390 US-listed ETF launches over the last 2 months, the largest 2-month increase on record.

This figure has more than tripled since the start of 2024.

As a result, more ETFs have launched over the last 2 months than during the entire first half of 2024.

Of all ETFs introduced this year, 54% incorporate derivatives, and over 33% are classified as leveraged or inverse funds.

Furthermore, fund issuers have already filed for more than 1,000 leveraged ETFs so far this year, pointing to another wave of launches ahead.

The ETF market is expanding faster than ever.

Asia's leverage boom is rapidly reversing:

Margin debt in South Korea has declined -$4 billion from its June peak, to $22 billion, the lowest since mid-April.

At the same time, stock margin loans in China have dropped -$59 billion, to $385 billion, the lowest since the 2nd week of April.

Similarly, in Taiwan, margin debt has fallen -$4 billion from its July peak, to $15 billion, the lowest since mid-May.

Combined, margin debt across these three markets has declined by a massive -$67 billion.

On top of that, South Korea-listed leveraged ETFs linked to SK Hynix and Samsung have lost -$7 billion in assets since their June peak, down -63%, to $4 billion.

Leverage is amplifying historic volatility across Asian markets.

Why you are not seeing volume on my charts

Following a breakout, it is impossible to know how long it will take (or even, if it will) for the price to reach the pattern objective. There is no rule or guideline in the literature on this. 

Ideally stops can be raised from below the pattern boundary to below the latest consolidation once price starts moving higher again. (this is if you are not applying any mechanical trailing stop).

#ascendingtriangle is a bullish chart pattern. It can form as a continuation as well as a bottom reversal. It's upward sloping lower boundary gives the pattern the bullish bias. Patterns are repetitive irrespective of time, geography, exchange or instrument.   

This ascending triangle is from 1986. Peter Brand's identification of a bottom reversal.  From his book Trading Commodity Futures with Classical Chart Patters.

The US housing market is in for a wild ride.

As rates rise to new highs, the average interest rate on a 30Y Mortgage is nearing 7%.

In other words, if you bought a home in 2021 at 3% interest, moving to a new home today would increase your rate by ~400 basis points.

Assuming you buy a $500,000 home with 20% down:

1. Monthly Payment at 3% Interest: $1,686/mo
2. Monthly Payment at 7% Interest: $2,661/mo

That's an increase of almost $1,000/mo, or +58%.

The already stagnant housing market is set to freeze.
